description: Webhook deduplication table with UNIQUE(provider, event_id) constraint, provider/event_id/event_type columns, and proper indexes
steps: Step 1: Run SQL query via Supabase: SELECT column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='processed_events'
Step 2: Verify columns exist: id (uuid), provider (varchar), event_id (varchar), event_type (varchar), processed_at (timestamptz), status_code (integer)
Step 3: Verify UNIQUE constraint on (provider, event_id) via: SELECT conname FROM pg_constraint WHERE conrelid='processed_events'::regclass AND contype='u'
Step 4: Verify index idx_processed_events_provider exists

description: Cron execution tracking table with status CHECK constraint and proper schema for mutual exclusion tracking
steps: Step 1: Run SQL query: SELECT column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_name='cron_runs'
Step 2: Verify columns: id (uuid), cron_name (varchar), started_at (timestamptz), finished_at (timestamptz), status (varchar), duration_ms (integer), error_message (text), rows_affected (integer)
Step 3: Verify CHECK constraint on status: IN ('running','completed','failed','skipped')
Step 4: Verify index idx_cron_runs_name_started exists

description: Return lifecycle table with full status lifecycle columns and proper foreign keys

Step 2: Verify columns: id, order_id, customer_id, status, reason, admin_notes, return_tracking_number, refund_amount_cents, created_at, updated_at, resolved_at, resolved_by
Step 3: Verify CHECK constraint on status: IN ('return_requested','return_approved','item_shipped','item_received','return_completed','rejected','expired')
Step 4: Verify FK references to orders(id) and users(id)
Step 5: Verify indexes idx_returns_order and idx_returns_status exist

description: Orders table has stripe_refund_id (UNIQUE), refunded_at, refund_amount_cents, refund_reason, retry_count columns

Step 2: Verify all 5 columns exist with correct types
Step 3: Verify UNIQUE constraint on stripe_refund_id
Step 4: Verify retry_count has DEFAULT 0

description: PostgreSQL function atomically processes refunds and returns FALSE for already-refunded orders
steps: Step 1: Verify function exists: SELECT proname FROM pg_proc WHERE proname='issue_refund_atomic'
Step 2: Verify function is SECURITY DEFINER
Step 3: Test: Call with a valid order → returns TRUE, sets refunded_at
Step 4: Test: Call again on same order → returns FALSE (already refunded)

description: PostgreSQL function returns BOOLEAN for advisory lock acquisition, FALSE when lock held by another session
steps: Step 1: Verify function exists: SELECT proname FROM pg_proc WHERE proname='try_cron_lock'
Step 2: Test: Call try_cron_lock('test_cron') → returns TRUE
Step 3: Test: In same transaction, verify lock prevents second acquisition
